findings.title: Task 1 fixture lines cannot yield Task 5's asserted results and break existing fixture tests
findings.description:
There are three defects in the Task 1 / Task 5 fixture plan:

- **Unindexed example never matches.** The line `7. [~] Feature Epsilon without explicit index — cut for scope.` has no `**Name**` bold wrap, and `PLAN_UNINDEXED_RE` (`packages/core/src/introspection/parsers/slicePlanParser.ts:9`) requires `\*\*`. After Task 2 it is still dropped, so Task 5's `totalSlices: 7`, `completedSlices: 5` and `indexSource: 'fallback'` assertions fail. The slice design's own form is `N. [~] **Name** — rationale`.
- **A bolded unindexed line reorders the fixture.** It would get fallback index `1` and sort ahead of 101 (`slicePlanParser.ts:91`). That shifts `result.entries[0]` and `[2]` and breaks `toHaveLength(5)` in `packages/core/tests/introspection/slicePlanParser.test.ts:10-30`. Task 5 only updates the totals test at lines 42-46.
- **Another test reads the same fixture.** `packages/core/tests/introspection/ArtifactIntrospector.test.ts:52` asserts `totalSlices` is 5 on `sample-slice-plan.md`. No task updates it, so Task 5's commit lands with a red suite that only Task 13 would catch.

Editing the shared fixture also contradicts the slice criterion that `[ ]`/`[x]`/`[X]` behavior is "proven by the existing `sample-slice-plan.md` fixture tests continuing to pass unchanged".

Fix: use the sibling-fixture option the slice design allows (e.g. a new `deprecated-slice-plan.md` with a bolded indexed and a bolded unindexed `[~]` line). Leave `sample-slice-plan.md` and its tests untouched, and drop the "update existing totals test" step and the separate regression test from Task 5.

findings.title: Task 8 misstates the caller of `resolveEntryStatus`
findings.description: Task 8 says the only caller "passes a full `SlicePlanEntry`". The actual caller is `resolveEntryStatusSafe`, whose own parameter is `Pick<SlicePlanEntry, 'index' | 'isChecked'>`. Widening only `resolveEntryStatus`'s `Pick` fails typecheck at line 740. Task 8 should say to widen both signatures.

findings.title: Task 9's `derivedStatus` initializer change rests on a wrong premise and is outside the slice
findings.description: The task claims the initializer is "the fallback used if `detectDocuments` throws". It is not: the `catch` at lines 125-127 sets `derivedStatus = 'degraded'`, and the success path always reassigns at line 122. The initializer value is never observed, so the change is dead code. The slice design scopes `slice.ts` to "the same one-line addition" only. Cut this sub-item.

findings.title: Task 12 is tautological against mocked plan results and omits `arch-status-vs-plans`
findings.description:
The existing `plan-status-vs-entries` and `arch-status-vs-plans` tests mock `parseSlicePlan` with hand-written `totalSlices`/`completedSlices`. A case "where every entry is `[x]` or `[~]`" would just set the two numbers equal by hand, which the existing all-complete cases already cover. It says nothing about Decision 3.

The real proof is a parser-level test, and it is missing: Task 4's success condition (all checked-or-`[~]` gives `completedSlices === totalSlices`) is never asserted in Task 5.

Fix: add that all-resolved assertion to Task 5. Then either cut Task 12 or have it feed a real `parseSlicePlan()` result into the checker for both rules named in the success criterion.

findings.title: Commit markers are checkboxes, and the first lands at an untested point
findings.description:
All six commit markers are written as `- [ ] Commit: …` checkbox sub-items (lines 105, 135, 179, 197, 212, 224). They should be plain `**Commit**:` lines.

The Task 5 marker is gated only on the filtered `slicePlanParser` run, which misses the `ArtifactIntrospector` breakage described above. Task 13's conditional "commit if anything remains" marker should be removed; verification-pass fixes belong in the commit of the task they correct.

findings.title: Task count is heavy for the size of the change
findings.description:
There are thirteen tasks for roughly ten lines of production change across four files.

- **Merge Tasks 2, 3 and 4.** They touch one function in one file and none is independently testable.
- **Merge Tasks 8 and 9.** They make the identical one-line wiring change at two call sites.
- **Drop the "do not change X" sub-items.** They restate the slice design and are not completable checklist items (lines 57, 80-81, 115-117).

findings.title: MCP worktree-filtered path recomputes `completedSlices` without the deprecated rule
findings.description: When an `indexRange` applies, this tool recomputes `completedSlices` with `e.isChecked` only. A `[~]` entry will count as resolved from the parser but not on this path. The slice design does not list this file, so it is a design-level gap, not a task omission; it also duplicates the predicate Task 4 changes.

findings.title: Success criteria are traceable to tasks
findings.description:
- **Indexed and unindexed parsing:** Tasks 2, 3 and 5.
- **Totals arithmetic:** Tasks 4 and 5.
- **`cf list slices` rendering and no `← next`:** Tasks 6-10.
- **`cf next` skip:** Task 11.
- **ConsistencyChecker:** Task 12 (weakly, per the concern above).
- **Regression-free `[ ]`/`[x]`/`[X]`:** Task 5.

No NFR is restated in the slice, so no load-test or CI-gating task is required.

findings.title: Sequencing and test-with pattern
findings.description: Dependencies run forward only: parser, then derivation signal, then wiring, then CLI and navigator verification. Each implementation group is immediately followed by its test task (5 after 2-4, 7 after 6, 10 and 11 after 8-9). File paths and line references for `statusDerivation.ts`, `WorkflowNavigator.ts:692` and `slice.ts:91/124` match the code.
